Non-classical Monocytes.description: Non-classical monocytes (CD14lowCD16+) are patrolling monocytes that survey the vasculature and are involved in inflammation resolution, expressing high levels of FCGR3A and CX3CR1.

Classical Monocytes.description: Classical monocytes (CD14+CD16-) are the most abundant monocyte subset, highly phagocytic and expressing high levels of CD14 and S100 family proteins.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells are innate lymphocytes that provide rapid responses against infected or stressed cells, characterized by expression of NKG7, GNLY, and perforin.

Intermediate Monocytes.description: Intermediate monocytes (CD14+CD16+) exhibit both classical and non-classical features, with high antigen-presenting capacity and pro-inflammatory cytokine production.

Switched memory B cell.description: Memory B cell that has undergone class switching, expressing IgG, IgA, or IgE and CD27, involved in recall responses.

Unswitched memory B cell.description: Memory B cell retaining IgM and IgD expression with CD27, representing early memory responses.

Naive B cell.description: Mature B cell that has not yet encountered antigen, characterized by high IgD and IgM, CD27 negativity, and CD23 expression.

Plasma cell.description: Terminally differentiated B cell responsible for antibody secretion, characterized by high expression of CD38, CD138, and transcription factors such as PRDM1 and XBP1.
